reason: The cited evidence supports that lattice distortions and porosity each lower thermal conductivity, but no evidence is provided for a predictive model that combines these effects or for the claimed improvement over conventional models; the hypothesis overstates the support by citing general observations rather than model validation.
premises: High-entropy lattice distortions reduce phonon mean free path and intrinsic thermal conductivity
Dual-porosity structures further reduce thermal conductivity via additional phonon scattering
Mass and strain field fluctuations are key mechanisms for phonon scattering in HEAs
Conventional Callaway–Debye or ideal solution models are insufficient for predicting κL in these systems
A model incorporating both disorder and porosity effects will yield significantly lower and more accurate κL predictions
